I am 55, I never went to school. I learned all this from my mother and from watching the neighbors. I have 8.2 mu. I put 5 mu in wheat and then maize after, and the other 3.2 mu I plant cotton. My son and daughter work in a factory in Shijiazhuang, so they send money home, but that means less hands at home. When harvest comes, I hire people to help.

For the wheat: Last year I put one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer — the kind with 15-15-15 written on the bag — on each mu when I planted, and then one 50-jin bag of urea on each mu when the wheat started jointing. This year I will do exactly the same. I will water three times: once before winter, once when it warms up in spring, and once when the heads come out. I spray twice for aphids. I expect about 500 kg per mu, same as last year if the weather holds.

For the maize: After I cut the wheat in June, I hire the machine to rotary till the field quick, then I plant the maize. I use hybrid seed, the same kind Old Li used last year — his ears were big. For each mu I put down one bag of compound and one bag of urea. I water twice if the rain doesn't come. I spray once for armyworm. I hope for 600 kg per mu.

For the cotton: I plant at the end of April. Cotton is hungry, so I plough deep and put down one and a half bags of compound and one bag of urea per mu. I water three times: once when I plant, once when the yellow flowers open, and once when the bolls are fat. I spray four times for bollworm and red spider. Picking is hard on my back, so I hire three women from the village for a week. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I know fertilizer is expensive — one bag of compound is 180 yuan, urea is 110 yuan — but I would rather put a bit too much than lose the crop. A bad harvest is a disaster. Last year my neighbor Wang tried to save money on cotton fertilizer and his bolls were small. I copy what works.
